title: The effectiveness of a preconditioning programme on preventing running-related injuries in novice runners: a randomised controlled trial
authors: Bredeweg SW, Zijlstra S, Bessem B, Buist I
population: Novice runners preparing for a four-mile event (Netherlands)
findings: 432 novices were allocated to a 4-week preconditioning (PRECON) programme of walking and hopping exercises (n=211) or control (n=221); both groups then did a 9-week running programme.
Primary outcome, running-related injuries per 100 runners: 15.2% (PRECON) vs 16.8% (control), chi2=0.161, df=1, p=0.69, not significant.
Authors conclude a 4-week preconditioning programme with walking and hopping exercises had no influence on the incidence of running-related injuries in novice runners.
limitations: Walking-and-hopping preconditioning only (not run-walk); injury needed a restriction of running of at least a week; no arm testing run-walk against continuous running; the control group began running at once, but the start dose of the 9-week programme is not given in the abstract.
implications: A 4-week walking and hopping block before the first run did not lower injury: do not add a preconditioning block before run-walk on the strength of injury prevention (grade B for this one contrast).
The trial does not test the starting dose or run-walk, so it gives no value for the floor week.
